sec: Liver development · embryology, hepatoblast fate and Alagille syndrome

items.q: At which embryonic age does the proliferating endodermal bud of the liver appear, and from which structure?
opts: 3 to 4 weeks, from the ventral wall of the foregut
6 to 7 weeks, from the dorsal wall of the midgut
3 to 4 weeks, from the septum transversum
8 to 9 weeks, from the ventral wall of the hindgut
items.exp: The line reads 3-4 weeks for a proliferating endodermal bud arising from the ventral wall of the foregut. (Book p982)

items.q: Match each inductive signal with the source named beside it — 1) FGF 2) BMP 7 … A) Septum transversum, whose mesodermal origin forms the connective tissue framework of the liver B) Cardiogenic mesoderm
items.exp: Fibroblast growth factor comes from the cardiogenic mesoderm, while bone morphogenetic protein 7 comes from the septum transversum, the mesoderm that forms the liver's connective tissue framework. (Book p982)

items.q: Assess the two bud branches: I The cranial bud is also called the hepatic diverticulum and gives rise to cords of hepatoblast. II The inferior part of the caudal bud forms the gall bladder.
items.exp: The cranial or hepatic diverticulum branch does form hepatoblast cords, but the caudal bud splits the other way round, with the superior part becoming the gall bladder and the inferior part the cystic duct and ventral pancreas. (Book p982)

items.q: Fill up: Hepatoblast cords invade the septum transversum because of a loss of the adhesion molecule ______.
items.exp: The invasion step is annotated as being due to loss of E-cadherin, printed here in the book's style for the epsilon form of the letter E. (Book p982)

items.q: Match each transcription factor with the fate it drives from the bipotential hepatoblast — 1) HNF-4 alpha 2) SOX-9 … A) Bile duct epithelial cell or cholangiocyte, with a raised Jagged1 and NOTCH pathway over TGF beta B) Hepatocyte, marked by CK8 and CK18
items.exp: HNF-4 alpha pushes the hepatoblast towards a hepatocyte fate carrying the cytokeratin markers CK8 and CK18, while SOX-9, acting through a dominant Jagged1 and NOTCH pathway over TGF beta, gives the cholangiocyte. (Book p982)

items.q: Which substance is shown as secreted by the bipotential hepatoblast at the branch point?
items.exp: The arrow leaving the hepatoblast is labelled secrete with AFP, alpha-fetoprotein, beneath it, and the plus sign shows that secretion feeding both branches. (Book p982)

items.q: Assess the two cytokeratin notes: I Glandular and transitional epithelium are named as the normal sites of cytokeratin expression. II Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is given as an example where cytokeratin appears as a tumour marker.
items.exp: The note splits normal expression into glandular and transitional epithelium and tumour expression into SCC of the lung, labelled as the SCC marker. (Book p982)

items.q: Fill up: Alagille syndrome is described as a defect of the ______ pathway and it is inherited in an ______ manner.
items.exp: The two opening bullets for Alagille syndrome read a Jagged1 and NOTCH2 pathway defect and autosomal dominant inheritance, which is the cholangiocyte branch of the same developmental pathway. (Book p982)

items.q: The hepatic feature of Alagille syndrome is intrahepatic bile duct paucity causing cholestasis. By what age is this expected to present?
items.exp: The first presentation bullet reads intrahepatic bile duct paucity leading to cholestasis with the annotation of under 6 months of birth. (Book p982)

items.q: All of these features belong to the characteristic facies of Alagille syndrome EXCEPT:
items.exp: The facies line lists a prominent forehead, deep set eyes, hypertelorism and a saddle nose, and the accompanying sketch shows exactly that coarse facies; micrognathia with cleft palate is not part of it. (Book p982)

items.q: Which ocular finding is listed as the ophthalmic feature, and shown in the coloured slit-lamp photograph?
items.exp: The fourth presentation bullet is posterior embryotoxon, illustrated beside the chest film of pulmonary stenosis on this page. (Book p982)

items.q: Match each Alagille presentation bullet with its organ system — 1) Butterfly vertebra 2) Renal obstruction 3) Mental retardation … A) Musculoskeletal B) Neurological C) Urinary
items.exp: The list continues on the next page with mental retardation, the characteristic facies, the ophthalmic and cardiac items, butterfly vertebra under musculoskeletal and renal obstruction as the seventh entry. (Book p982)

items.q: Assess the pathway logic of this page: I Alagille syndrome affects the SOX-9 driven branch of hepatoblast differentiation. II Hepatocyte markers in this scheme are CK8 and CK18, the same cytokeratins the note links to glandular epithelium.
items.exp: Bile duct paucity in Alagille follows the Jagged1 and NOTCH-driven cholangiocyte branch under SOX-9, and the hepatocyte markers listed are CK8 and CK18, tying the developmental note to the cytokeratin note beneath it. (Book p982)

items.q: A 3-month-old has conjugated cholestasis, a prominent forehead with hypertelorism, a systolic ejection murmur and a butterfly vertebra on spine films. Which developmental pathway is disrupted?
opts: Jagged1 and NOTCH2 signalling in cholangiocyte differentiation
BMP 7 signalling from the septum transversum
items.exp: The cluster of bile duct paucity, facies, cardiac murmur and butterfly vertebra is the Alagille presentation on this page, and its stated basis is a Jagged1 or NOTCH2 pathway defect, the same signal that pushes hepatoblasts towards cholangiocytes. (Book p982)
